findings.summary: The harness reads bblite_core's C++ standard and its MSVC and clang-cl options from native/CMakeLists.txt instead of keeping two hand-written copies of them.
/nologo belongs to the runner, not the product options; a link-only command passes through unchanged.

The guard rejects everything the harness owns: warning levels and per-warning switches (/w, /wd, -W, /clang:-W), /Zc, /fp, /utf-8 and the charsets, /external:W and :env, and the product include folders.
A command compiles when it names any C or C++ source spelling (.c, .cxx, /Tp, /Tc); the guard and the macro loop read only the arguments before /link.
Restated /external:W0, the default /fp:precise, and the /fp:strict and /utf-8 the product does not build with are removed, so fixtures prove the product's float model and charset.
The harness owns native/include and the dependency headers, searched after a fixture's own folders as CMake orders interface includes; 548 hand-written spellings are removed.
Restated linker and compiler defaults are removed: /Gy under /O2 and /OPT:REF without /DEBUG.

96 hand-built generated-program checks (check.cpp in an artifacts folder, one compile, one run) call runGeneratedProgram, whose single flags option replaces defines and includeDirectories; checks that run in their own folder, trim the output or read files afterwards stay explicit.

The RmlUi fixtures compile pal_system_fonts.cpp and RmlUi_Platform_SDL.cpp, which read no fixture macro, under one fixed command each, so every fixture after the first restores those objects from the cache instead of recompiling them.
The development guide points at the CMake source instead of copying the flag list, and the paragraph is reflowed.
A unit test checks the derived options, the include order, link-only pass-through and the guard without a compiler, so a restatement is caught on every machine.
